articles.title: Six killed in Israeli airstrike on Gaza’s Nasser Hospital
articles.summary: An Israeli airstrike on Gaza’s Nasser Hospital on Wednesday night killed six people, injured 27 others and caused extensive damage.

articles.title: Gaza winter aid: ‘No more delay’, Fletcher tells governments stalling on support
articles.summary: The UN’s Emergency Relief Coordinator, Tom Fletcher, expressed deep concern about the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Gaza, as UN member states and partners have been repeatedly delaying sending their support to the Strip.

articles.title: World News in Brief: Ending cholera by 2030 ‘within reach’, Haiti displacement and hunger, US human rights review rescheduled
articles.summary: Ending cholera as a public health threat by 2030 is within reach, as every cholera death can be prevented with tools that already exist, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: At least 56 migrants die in weekend shipwrecks off Senegal and Greece
articles.summary: At least 56 people died in a series of shipwrecks off Senegal and Greece over the weekend, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said on Monday, calling it a stark reminder of the deadly risks they face on the Atlantic and Mediterranean.

articles.title: Beyond the broken glass: The human cost of the 1938 November Pogrom
articles.summary: On his way to school in Vienna on the morning of 10 November 1938, eight-year-old Arthur Schneier watched his synagogue burn while firefighters and police officers stood by “rejoicing”.

articles.title: ‘For the first time I have my own chair’: Gaza siblings find new freedom
articles.summary: In Gaza, 10-year-old Anas is one of three siblings born without legs and with only two fingers on each of their hands. They struggle to move around and perform daily activities like eating and writing independently.

articles.title: Afghanistan faces deepening humanitarian crisis amid sweeping rights restrictions
articles.summary: Afghanistan stands at a “difficult crossroad” more than five years after the Taliban returned to power, a senior UN official said on Friday. Relative stability and security are being undercut by a fragile economy, sweeping curbs on rights and acute humanitarian need.
